title: Introduce lightweight context carrier and export throttling
creator: Anika Patel
description: Background: Our runtime continues to pay a high CPU and allocation toll in the hotpath when attaching full trace baggage and fanout to multiple exporters. This is visible in p99 CPU spikes during bursty workloads and in tail latency regressions in the token path. Goal: Implement a compact, immutable 'context carrier' (minimal header payload + pre-serialized KV fragments) used inside the runtime hotpath and add an export throttling circuit that limits exporter fanout and buffers when remote endpoints are congested. The aim is to reduce per-request allocations by ~40%, lower p99 latency under burst by 20%, and avoid exporter-driven backlog amplification.
design_notes: - Context carrier: single flat byte buffer with TLV-ish layout (key id, length, value) to avoid map allocations. Carrier created once per request and passed by reference. - Sampling heuristics: prefer early-sampling decisions; add cheap fingerprint to avoid re-hydrating heavy baggage for low-sampled traces. - Export throttling: token-bucket + short-term ring buffer per-exporter + observable backpressure metric. If exporter lag exceeds threshold, automatically route to secondary aggregator or drop non-critical spans. - Safety: preserve full fidelity in debug mode (env RH_OBS_FULL_TRACE=1) and for tracing-enabled customers. - Trade-offs: small CPU cost to serialize to carrier vs larger cost saved from eliminating map copies; potential incompatibility with some non-Redwood exporter adapters -> adapters will be updated to accept carrier or there is a compatibility shim.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Hotpath allocations for trace attach reduced >=30% in microbenchmarks. 2) End-to-end p99 tail latency improved by >=15% in synthetic burst tests. 3) Exporter queue depth metrics expose throttling events and fallbacks. 4) No functional change for customers with tracing turned on; debug/full mode still emits full baggage. 5) Unit + property tests for carrier parsing and exporter backpressure behavior present.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: PoC carrier and perf bench in isolated runtime crate; confirm allocations and latencies. Phase 2: Implement carrier in runtime hotpath and add exporter throttling in fanout layer. Phase 3: Add compat shim for existing exporters and land adapters PRs. Phase 4: Gradual rollout behind feature flag (obs.carrier=true) starting with canary fleet and monitor. Phase 5: Roll forward, enable by default, and publish migration notes.
risks_and_mitigations: - Risk: Carrier parsing bug could drop critical baggage -> mitigation: conservative feature-flag rollout and parity tests against current baggage. - Risk: Throttling causes data loss for high-fidelity customers -> mitigation: metrics, alerts, and opt-out flags; route to long-term storage instead of silent drop for configured tenants. - Risk: Third-party exporter compatibility -> mitigation: provide compatibility shim and immediate PRs to top-5 adapters.
monitoring_and_metrics: New metrics to add: telemetry.carrier.alloc_delta (gauge), exporter.<name>.throttle_events (counter), exporter.<name>.queue_depth (gauge), telemetry.hotpath_p99_ms (histogram). Dashboards: carrier adoption, per-exporter throttle rate, error regressions, and end-to-end trace completeness rate.
rollout_plan: - Week 0: Merge behind feature flag, enable in internal dev cluster. - Week 1: Canary on 5% of runtime hosts, short-lived bursts. - Week 2: 25% rollout with export throttling enabled, monitor for dropped spans. - Week 4: 100% enable with compatibility shims in place. - Post-rollout: 2-week watch and rollback window.
